design.reasoning: Saturate scaled percentage when >= Double(Int.max); equality must be caught because the 64-bit upper bound rounds to 2^63. Immutable clamped inputs make the percentage nonnegative and finite.
design.class_inventory: No second reachable occurrence of this unbounded-percentage conversion. Related percentile casts are bounded by allocated collection counts; one other percentage conversion uses fixed test ratios.
limits: Read-only source and Python binary64 arithmetic; no Swift runs by reviewer.

final.result: No actionable findings; source and regression design approved, pending full validation.
verified_by_source: The >= guard catches 64-bit equality rounded to 2^63.
Clamped immutable inputs and the zero-total guard make scaled finite and nonnegative.
The below-boundary integer expectation catches premature saturation; equality cases catch an unsafe > guard.
13 input-range rows and 4 conversion-boundary rows cover negative clamping, zero totals and extremes; ordinary expectations preserve 150,33,66.
Ordinary import VectorCore covers public access.
Changelog, BH-67, CL-77 and VC-AUDIT-F007 agree with implementation.
limits: Reviewer did not rerun Swift tests.
Release and full validation were pending at review time.
No assertion of runtime validation on 32-bit or every supported Apple platform.

lead_completion: Full Debug, Release and final Python policies passed; existing skips and Release compiler canary retained.
ruling: Saturate only the unrepresentable floating percentage; retain overshoot and Double rounding. Consumers needing exact huge integer-rational percentages need a different representation.
